_meta.title: TRIVERSE timeline, published event data
_meta.source: The TRIVERSE codex, the unpublished worldbuilding reference of the novel series by Luis Blanco, restricted to premise-level and structural canon and the setup of Book 1 (chapter introductions only). Real-history and science items cite their published sources.
_meta.licence: TRIVERSE and its codex: Luis Blanco, all rights reserved. Not for reuse.

events.title: Something begins to live in the Vortex
events.text: The codex dates the Inhabitants of the Vortex to about four billion years. They are vast, ancient and hard for human minds to scale. At the story present no humanity knows what they intend.
events.sec: WHAT HUMANS EXPERIENCE IN VORTEX [CANON], Sensory Vocabulary

events.title: One species, three dimensions
events.text: Homo sapiens. The codex holds the three expression dimensions to the same species, the same DNA and the same cognitive architecture. They are separate dimensions, never one past that splits; what differs later is when each found its artifact.

events.title: The Holocene begins
events.text: The present interglacial begins about 11,700 years before 2000 CE, dated in the Greenland ice. Farming spreads in the Near East soon after.

events.title: Neolithic communities, in step
events.text: Earth at about 8000 BCE, in the codex’s master timeline: Neolithic communities in the Fertile Crescent. Our own history, and the stage every lane shares at this date.

events.title: Neolithic communities, in step
events.text: Terra at about 8000 BCE: Neolithic communities on its Mediterranean-equivalent coasts, at the same stage as Earth’s.

events.title: Kha-Ren finds its artifact
events.text: A Pre-Pottery Neolithic community of perhaps 200 to 500 people, at the confluence of the rivers Seren and Kelar in the Valorian basin of Upper Mesopotamia, finds a three-metre sphere set in limestone. Its surface holds at -3 °C. It hums at 110 Hz, 138 dB at the surface, and water condenses on it every day. This is the earliest discovery of the three.

events.title: Engagement, then catastrophe
events.text: The first communities try to engage with what they found: practices to strengthen perception, specialists to interpret it. It works for a while. Then something goes catastrophically wrong, and everything after is built around one lesson: no single person may hold the whole picture.

events.title: Access restricted
events.text: The artifact is sealed and access is restricted to the few who know how to approach it.
events.sec: PHASE 2: THE CONTAINMENT RESPONSE, row ~8000-7000 BCE

events.title: The frost moves with the sound
events.text: Ice gathers where the air around the artifact is still, at the nodes of its standing wave, and is swept away where the air oscillates. The ground carries a pattern. The codex makes this Kha-Ren’s first mathematics.
events.sec: C2.0 "The frost moves with the sound" (~7500 BCE)

events.title: Copper beside the sphere
events.text: Native copper is cold-hammered near the artifact: the start of a metallurgy chain in which work done inside the sound comes out stronger.
events.sec: C3.0 Native copper cold-hammered near artifact (~7500 BCE)

events.title: Nodes found by ear
events.text: People learn to locate the nodes of the standing wave by listening.
events.sec: C2.1 Standing wave node location by ear (~7000 BCE)

events.title: Fired pottery
events.text: Pottery reaches Upper Mesopotamia, as radiocarbon dates it on Earth at sites such as Tell Sabi Abyad. Fired ceramic tubes become possible.
events.sec: C1.0 Pottery available in Upper Mesopotamia (~7000 BCE)

events.title: The Sacred Songs
events.text: A first priestly class appears, and the Sacred Songs are codified: procedures for living beside the artifact, encoded as acoustic structures.
events.sec: PHASE 2: THE CONTAINMENT RESPONSE, row ~7000-6000 BCE

events.title: A fire in a tube sings
events.text: With fired ceramic tubes, Kha-Ren finds that a heated tube makes sound by itself. It is the first link in a chain that runs from fire to sound to power to cooling.

events.title: Beats heard
events.text: Two resonators slightly out of tune beat against each other. Listening for the beat gives sub-percent precision without any instrument.

events.title: The 8.2 ka cold event
events.text: An abrupt cold, dry spell about 8,200 years ago, recorded on Earth in the Greenland ice. The codex keeps Earth’s climate history in Kha-Ren’s world and makes this the pressure that hardened its social order.
events.sec: E-03 findings: the 8.2 ka event as forge

events.title: Society reorganises around the artifact
events.text: Specialist classes solidify around managing the artifact.
events.sec: PHASE 2: THE CONTAINMENT RESPONSE, row ~6000-5500 BCE

events.title: Length tunes the pitch
events.text: Tube length and pitch are optimised together, with thin, repeatable ceramic forms.

events.title: Knowledge divided
events.text: Knowledge distribution is formalised: different groups hold different pieces.
events.sec: PHASE 2: THE CONTAINMENT RESPONSE, row ~5500-5000 BCE

events.title: Better castings near the sound
events.text: Metal cast near the artifact is consistently better than metal cast elsewhere.
events.sec: C3.1 Castings near artifact consistently superior (~5000 BCE)

events.title: Ratios from overtones
events.text: Overtones teach whole-number ratios, 2:1, 3:2 and 4:3, between about 5000 and 4000 BCE.
events.sec: C2.2 Ratio theory from overtones (~5000-4000 BCE)

events.title: Cycle 1, Year 0: the castes
events.text: Four castes are formalised and Kha-Ren’s calendar begins. The seventeen Sacred Songs are frozen in exact pronunciation. Knowledge is divided among the castes so no single person holds enough to be destroyed by it, and the tradition stays oral. A Cycle is 75 years, about one lifetime.
events.sec: PHASE 3: THE CASTE CRYSTALLIZATION (~4675 BCE / Cycle 1, Year 0)

events.title: Stone becomes a channel
events.text: The first corridor: a cut-and-cover limestone channel that carries tapped signals through the bedrock. By the story present the codex gives the network 15,000 to 20,000 km, with a full alert in 33 seconds.
events.sec: C2.1a Corridor voice network physics (first corridor ~4000 BCE)

events.title: Rhythmic hammering
events.text: Rhythmic hammering is found to improve castings. The codex marks this date with a question mark.
events.sec: C3.2 Rhythmic hammering discovered to improve castings (~4000 BCE?)

events.title: Bronze resonators
events.text: Bronze resonators and copper heat exchangers replace ceramic.
events.sec: C1.3 Bronze resonators + copper heat exchangers (~3500 BCE)

events.title: The castes are 1,100 years old
events.text: When Terra finds its artifact, Kha-Ren’s castes are about 1,100 years old. The codex table gives Cycle 15 for this date; its own conversion formula gives Cycle 16, Year 13. Both are listed under the canon discrepancies.

events.title: Clicks leave everyday speech
events.text: Around Cycle 20, click consonants fall out of everyday speech. They survive only in the Sacred Register, which is still pronounced as it was in 4675 BCE.
events.sec: KEY HISTORICAL EVENTS, Last click speaker (vernacular)

events.title: The corridor reaches 200 km
events.text: The stone network runs about 200 km.
events.sec: C2.1a corridor timeline (200 km by 3000 BCE)

events.title: Sine waves made audible
events.text: A proto-trigonometry grows from sine waves that can be heard, between about 3000 and 2000 BCE.
events.sec: C2.4 Proto-trigonometry from sine waves made audible (~3000-2000 BCE)

events.title: The hidden source
events.text: Kha-Ren scholars measure the artifact’s sound and the ice it melts, then wrap it. It stays at -3 °C anyway. Energy comes out with nothing going in, and they formally propose a hidden source.

events.title: Sound that cools
events.text: Run in reverse, the sound engines pump heat away: sound becomes cooling.
events.sec: C1.4 Reverse effect: sound to cooling (~2500 BCE)

events.title: The 4.2 ka drought
events.text: An abrupt aridification about 2200 BCE that emptied settlements on the plains of northern Mesopotamia on Earth. In Kha-Ren it forces qanat-cistern irrigation and food preservation, and Kha-Ren becomes a refuge for its neighbours.

events.title: Fire that makes cold
events.text: Practical fire-driven food coolers.
events.sec: C1.5 Practical fire-driven food coolers (~2000 BCE)

events.title: Sound taken apart
events.text: Banks of tuned resonators split a sound into its frequencies: an empirical Fourier analysis, between about 2500 and 1500 BCE.
events.sec: C2.5 Empirical Fourier via Helmholtz resonator banks (~2500-1500 BCE)

events.title: Cooling to carry
events.text: Portable ceramic-bronze cooling devices make cold a trade good.
events.sec: C1.6 Portable ceramic-bronze hybrid devices (~1500 BCE)

events.title: The corridor at full capability
events.text: The stone network reaches full capability between about 1500 and 1000 BCE.

events.title: Acoustic iron and steel
events.text: Vibration during solidification refines iron and steel as it refined bronze.

events.title: Cycle 50
events.text: When Terra reaches post-scarcity, Kha-Ren is in Cycle 50.

events.title: Pressure vessels
events.text: Sealed bronze vessels at 2 to 3 atmospheres triple the power of the sound engines.

events.title: Kha-Ren writes
events.text: Writing is adopted about 4,400 years after the castes were formalised. Law and commerce move into text; sacred acoustic knowledge stays mostly oral.

events.title: Spectral analysis
events.text: Empirical spectral analysis, between about 300 and 100 BCE.

events.title: Threads cut in bronze
events.text: Thread-cutting, between about 230 and 160 BCE, makes vessels at 5 to 50 atmospheres possible.

events.title: The looped engine
events.text: Kha-Ren builds a travelling-wave thermoacoustic engine around a looped tube. At 3 to 5 atmospheres it reaches 15 to 25 percent of the Carnot limit.

events.title: The fifth caste
events.text: A sequence of epidemics between about 200 and 500 CE forces recruitment across caste lines. The Amber caste emerges: specialists who hold both practical and theoretical knowledge.

events.title: The Reformation
events.text: Kha-Ren reforms without rejecting its artifact. The Acoustic Compact replaces Keeper autocracy with a written constitutional framework, the five-caste model is formalised, and apprenticeship rights for the Brown caste are written into law.

events.title: Cycle 90 begins
events.text: By the codex’s conversion, Cycle 90 begins in 2000 CE; the story present is its 68th year.

events.title: Cycle 90, Year 68
events.text: Kha-Ren at the story present: a divergent acoustic civilisation, ten thousand years of innovation without electrical industry, built on thermoacoustic engines, vibrational metallurgy and acoustic medicine. Caste is audible, because each caste speaks its own register. The capital, Valoria, is built in concentric rings by caste around the Sacred Circle, where the Keepers of Continuity hold the artifact.
events.sec: IDENTITY; WHAT MAKES KHA-REN DIFFERENT; KEY LOCATIONS

events.title: Nasha
events.text: Nasha, 17, a Green-caste weaver whose patterns the Keepers are watching.

events.title: The planet forms
events.text: Earth forms about 4.54 billion years ago. The codex dates the Vortex’s Inhabitants to about four billion years, half a billion years younger than the planet.

events.title: Lumina
events.text: Lumina, Terra’s capital, stands on the discovery site and has been lived in continuously for the 5,605 years since.

events.title: Sealed vessels behave differently
events.text: Capped bronze tubes are found to behave differently from open ones, between about 1500 and 1000 BCE: the first step toward pressurised engines.

events.title: Pressure and the loop together
events.text: Between about 50 BCE and 500 CE the pressurised vessel and the looped engine are combined, at 15 to 25 percent of the Carnot limit: the codex’s ceiling for Kha-Ren bronze.
events.sec: C1.7e Pressurized + traveling-wave combined (~50 BCE-500 CE)

events.title: Terra finds its artifact: 0 A.T.
events.text: On Terra’s Mediterranean-equivalent coast, workers rebuilding a collapsed library dig into a chamber that should not exist, and find the artifact. Terra’s calendar starts here, Year 0 After Terra. The society that finds it already has cities, writing and scholars, who first take it for a relic of an older civilisation.
events.sec: PHASE 1: ARTIFACT DISCOVERY (~3537 BCE / Year 0 A.T.)

events.title: Shared dreams
events.text: Those who study the artifact report shared dreams, sudden insight and thinking together. Within a generation they become a new intellectual elite, and in the first two centuries the study community grows into a proto-civilisation.
events.sec: PHASE 1: First Contact; PHASE 2, row 0-200 A.T.

events.title: The field spreads
events.text: Between about 200 and 500 A.T. the artifact’s cognitive effects reach beyond its vicinity. Many languages are still spoken, and violence is still common.
events.sec: PHASE 2: EARLY ARTIFACT ERA, row 200-500 A.T.

events.title: Science accelerates
events.text: Between about 500 and 800 A.T. Terran climate science, materials science and medicine advance by orders of magnitude.
events.sec: PHASE 2: EARLY ARTIFACT ERA, row 500-800 A.T.

events.title: Consolidation
events.text: From about 2000 to 2600 A.T. Terra settles into one language and one framework of thought, and climate engineering works at continental scale.

events.title: The artifact is moved
events.text: About three thousand years before the story present, Terra moves its artifact from the discovery site into a secured facility, where it has been studied ever since.

events.title: Post-scarcity
events.text: Around 2600 A.T. Terra ends material want, about three thousand years before Earth’s 2068.

events.title: Extinction halted
events.text: Around 2800 A.T. Terra stops extinction. From here every ecosystem is curated.

events.title: The last unmanaged storm
events.text: Around 3200 A.T. After it, Terra’s weather is managed.

events.title: Alexander turns to dimensional research
events.text: Alexander Bellamy begins the dimensional research he is doing when Book 1 opens.

events.title: 5605 A.T.
events.text: Terra at the story present: about 12 billion people living 300 years and more, no war, no poverty, managed weather and a complete dimensional physics that corrected its variable constants long ago. Light is sourceless and diffuse, so shadows do not know which way to fall. Governance is by consensus through Unified Thought, a cognitive framework the artifact made possible; the codex rules out telepathy and a hive mind. The capital is Lumina, and a Terran year is about 400 days.
events.sec: IDENTITY; WHAT MAKES TERRA DIFFERENT; UNIFIED THOUGHT, What It Is

events.title: Alexander Bellamy
events.text: A senior researcher at the Lumina Institute on Terra, doing dimensional research when Book 1 opens.

events.title: Sera, archivist
events.text: An archivist in Lumina, 67 by the Earth reckoning and 61 in Terran years.

events.title: Bronze Age civilisations
events.text: Earth at about 3537 BCE, the year Terra finds its artifact: Bronze Age civilisations, with no artifact found and none noticed.

events.title: Tapping the chest
events.text: Auenbrugger publishes percussion of the chest: tapping the body and listening to it. The codex cites this as the equivalent of Kha-Ren’s thirty-second acoustic triage, which it does not date.

events.title: The stethoscope
events.text: Laënnec listens to the chest through a rolled tube, the first stethoscope. The codex pairs it with Auenbrugger as Earth’s version of Kha-Ren’s acoustic diagnosis.

events.title: The mechanical equivalent of heat
events.text: Joule measures how much work makes a given amount of heat, the experimental footing of energy conservation. Kha-Ren balanced the same kind of books around 2500 BCE, because its artifact broke them.

events.title: Sondhauss: a heated tube sings
events.text: Sondhauss describes glass tubes that sing when heated at one end. Kha-Ren found the effect about 8,350 years earlier.

events.title: Helmholtz’s resonators
events.text: Helmholtz analyses sound with sets of tuned resonators, each answering one frequency.

events.title: Kundt’s tube
events.text: Kundt makes standing sound waves visible: fine powder in a resonating tube collects at the nodes.

events.title: Instruments flag a mesa
events.text: In the codex, instruments first register anomalies around a mesa in New Mexico. It is the first sign of Earth’s artifact.

events.title: A cavern below Mesa Oscura
events.text: Deep seismic mapping finds a natural volcanic cavern about 400 feet below Mesa Oscura in the Jemez Mountains.

events.title: Is the fine-structure constant constant?
events.text: Quasar spectra are reported to show the fine-structure constant slightly different in the early universe. The result is debated. In the codex, constants are local near dimensional boundaries, and Terra corrected for this long ago.

events.title: A looped heat engine
events.text: Backhaus and Swift build a travelling-wave thermoacoustic engine with no moving parts and 30 percent thermal efficiency. Kha-Ren’s looped engine is about 2,100 years older.

events.title: Clocks drift near the mesa
events.text: GPS timing anomalies appear in the Jemez region from the late 1990s. The official explanation is terrain interference. The codex’s is a local time dilation around the artifact.

events.title: The Higgs boson
events.text: The Higgs boson is found at the Large Hadron Collider. In the codex it is the last fundamental discovery before a long desert.

events.title: The present day
events.text: Where real history stops. Everything on Earth’s line to the right of this marker is the codex’s forecast.

events.title: A first fusion plant
events.text: In the codex’s forecast, the first operational fusion plant opens in France: expensive, not yet scalable.

events.title: Population peaks
events.text: Climate adaptation dominates policy and coasts retreat. The codex has world population peak at about 10.2 billion in 2030.

events.title: Earth reaches its artifact
events.text: The artifact beneath Mesa Oscura is accessed and studied in secret: a sphere about three metres across, dark grey to deep blue, shifting colour with the angle, patterns moving inside its surface, always -3 °C. It stays dormant, and Earth’s humanity is still unaltered by it.
events.sec: Earth Artifact — Oscura Cavern; SHARED PROPERTIES [CANON]

events.title: Quantum computers at work
events.text: Quantum computing reaches practical scale for cryptography and materials simulation.

events.title: The Standard Model, again
events.text: The Standard Model is confirmed to unprecedented precision, and the physics community’s despair deepens.

events.title: Oscura is announced
events.text: Oscura Laboratory is announced publicly as a joint US and EU project on the mesa.

events.title: A collider finds nothing new
events.text: In the codex, the Future Circular Collider at CERN begins operating and confirms the Standard Model. Nothing new.

events.title: Narrow AI everywhere
events.text: Narrow AI is everywhere and general AI has not arrived. The gap between known physics and anything new seems endless.

events.title: Higher energies, nothing new
events.text: China’s Circular Electron-Positron Collider reaches higher energies and finds nothing new.

events.title: Oscura opens
events.text: The laboratory becomes operational and begins work on accelerator physics.

events.title: Fusion pays
events.text: Fusion power becomes commercially viable but stays expensive; the grid is still mixed.

events.title: Bases on the Moon
events.text: Moon bases are established by the US, China and an EU consortium; Mars missions are in planning.

events.title: Gene therapy is routine
events.text: Gene therapy becomes routine for common conditions; average lifespan in developed nations is about 85.

events.title: Emily Chen joins Oscura’s ethics board
events.text: Emily Chen joins the Oscura Ethics Advisory Board.

events.title: Emily meets Samantha
events.text: Emily Chen meets Samantha Lee at a conference in Geneva.

events.title: Samantha and John start working together
events.text: The partnership Book 1 opens on is nine years old in 2068.

events.title: Grey Dynamics is founded
events.text: Martin Grey’s company, Grey Dynamics, is founded.

events.title: Samantha Lee joins Oscura
events.text: A quantum physicist, recruited to Oscura at 35.

events.title: Something in the data
events.text: Early 2068. Working late, Samantha Lee finds a pattern in her data that matches no model. Book 1 opens here.

events.title: 2068 CE
events.text: Earth at the story present: about 10 billion people, quantum computing for specialised tasks, narrow AI everywhere and no general AI, fusion arriving, bases on the Moon, and particle physics 56 years without a fundamental discovery. Its humanity is unaltered by its artifact. Earth’s divergence begins here.
events.sec: IDENTITY; TECHNOLOGY LEVEL; THE PHYSICS COMMUNITY

events.title: One now
events.text: At the story present the three worlds are synchronised: 2068 CE on Earth is 5605 A.T. on Terra and Cycle 90, Year 68 in Kha-Ren. The codex makes this a property of the substrate the three share. Earlier dates on this page are placed on Earth’s clock, as the codex places them.

eras.name: neolithic
eras.text: Neolithic communities in the Fertile Crescent, in step with Terra.

eras.name: neolithic
eras.text: Neolithic communities on Mediterranean-equivalent coasts, in step with Earth.

eras.name: bronze age
eras.text: Cities, writing and Bronze Age civilisations, in step with Terra until Terra’s discovery.

eras.name: bronze age
eras.text: An urban Bronze Age civilisation with writing and scholars, in step with Earth.

eras.name: containment
eras.text: Engagement, then catastrophe, then 3,300 years of building a social order around the artifact.

eras.name: the oral caste era
eras.text: Four castes, an oral tradition and the frozen Sacred Register, while five acoustic technology chains grow inside the constraints.

eras.name: writing to reform
eras.text: Writing transforms law and commerce; epidemics produce a fifth caste.

eras.name: the Compact
eras.text: Governance under the Acoustic Compact, a written constitutional framework, after the Reformation.

eras.name: early artifact era
eras.text: The artifact study community grows into a civilisation. Many languages are still spoken; violence is still common.

eras.name: consolidation
eras.text: One language and one framework of thought; climate engineering at continental scale.

eras.name: post-scarcity
eras.text: About three thousand years without war or want, with lifespans past three hundred years.

eras.name: iron to industry
eras.text: Our own history: iron, empires, print and science.

eras.name: industrial age
eras.text: Our own history: steam, electricity, the physics that built the Standard Model.

eras.name: information age
eras.text: Our own history: computers, networks, the Higgs boson.

eras.name: climate decade
eras.text: Adaptation dominates policy; the codex forecast begins.

eras.name: the stagnation
eras.text: The Standard Model is confirmed again and again and nothing new appears.

eras.name: quiet desperation
eras.text: Narrow AI everywhere, no general AI, colliders that find nothing.

eras.name: the opening
eras.text: The years just before Book 1 opens.

held.text: This millennium of Terran history is not on the public timeline.
Kha-Ren history after the Reformation is still being developed in the codex and is not published here; the present-day picture is.

p-brane.title: Branes in a bulk
p-brane.claim: Our universe may be a 3+1-dimensional membrane in a higher-dimensional bulk. Gravity reaches into the bulk; the other forces stay on the brane.

refs.title: Large Mass Hierarchy from a Small Extra Dimension
refs.author: Randall

refs.title: An Alternative to Compactification
refs.author: Randall

ext.text: The three expression worlds are three branes on one bulk; the Vortex and Haven are the geometry of that bulk.

p-brane.detail: Randall and Sundrum showed that a warped extra dimension can explain why gravity is so much weaker than the other forces, and that a brane can sit in an infinite bulk without the extra dimension showing up in everyday physics. No experiment has detected an extra dimension yet; collider searches have only set limits on them.

p-warp.title: Each brane keeps its own time
p-warp.claim: In Randall–Sundrum geometry the metric carries a warp factor, ds² = e^(−2|y|/ℓ) η dx dx + dy², so clocks on different branes run at different rates. There is no single bulk time.

refs.title: Large Mass Hierarchy from a Small Extra Dimension
refs.author: Randall

ext.text: The codex synchronises the three worlds at the story present through their shared substrate. Older dates are aligned to Earth’s clock by convention.

p-warp.detail: The warp factor falls exponentially with distance into the extra dimension, so the same process runs at different rates on branes at different depths. Two worlds on two branes have no shared clock unless something links them, which is why this page places every date on Earth’s clock and says where the codex itself aligns them.

p-defect.title: Topological defects
p-defect.claim: When a symmetry breaks in a phase transition, regions that chose differently leave stable defects where they meet: domain walls, cosmic strings, monopoles. Cosmic strings could carry current and close into stable loops.

refs.title: Topology of cosmic domains and strings
refs.author: Kibble

refs.title: Superconducting strings
refs.author: Witten

ext.text: Each artifact is a stabilised topological defect, an object of spacetime rather than an object in it, engineered by the Builders as infrastructure.

p-defect.detail: Kibble showed that a cooling universe must leave such defects behind, because regions too far apart to exchange signals cannot agree on how to break a symmetry. Witten showed that cosmic strings could carry current without resistance. None has been observed; cosmic strings remain a prediction searched for in gravitational waves and the microwave background.

p-casimir.title: Negative energy density is real
p-casimir.claim: The Casimir force between closely spaced surfaces was measured to within about 5 percent of theory.

refs.title: Demonstration of the Casimir Force in the 0.6 to 6 μm Range
refs.author: Lamoreaux

ext.text: The artifact shifts colour with the viewing angle through Casimir-like effects at its boundary.

p-casimir.detail: Two uncharged metal plates a fraction of a micrometre apart are pushed together because the vacuum between them supports fewer electromagnetic modes than the vacuum outside. Lamoreaux measured the force with a torsion pendulum. It shows that empty space carries measurable energy that geometry can change, the idea the codex builds the artifact’s surface on.

p-zeno.title: Watching changes the outcome
p-zeno.claim: Frequent measurement freezes the evolution of a quantum system (the Zeno effect); some measurement schedules speed transitions up instead (anti-Zeno).

refs.cite: Itano, Heinzen, Bollinger & Wineland (1990), Physical Review A 41, 2295
refs.title: Quantum Zeno effect
refs.author: Itano

refs.cite: Fischer, Gutiérrez-Medina & Raizen (2001), Physical Review Letters 87, 040402
refs.title: Observation of the Quantum Zeno and Anti-Zeno Effects in an Unstable System
refs.author: Fischer

ext.text: The patterns inside every artifact speed up when watched and slow down when not, through a Zeno-type coupling.

p-zeno.detail: Itano and colleagues at NIST held trapped ions in one state by probing them with laser pulses: the more often they looked, the less the state changed. Raizen’s group then showed the opposite regime, in which measurement speeds a decay up. Observation is a physical interaction, not a passive record, which is what the codex borrows for an artifact that responds to being watched.

p-webb.title: Is the fine-structure constant constant?
p-webb.claim: Absorption lines in distant quasar spectra were reported to show α ≈ 1/137.036 slightly different in the early universe. The measurement is published; whether α really varies is still debated.

refs.cite: Webb, Flambaum, Churchill, Drinkwater & Barrow (1999), Physical Review Letters 82, 884
refs.title: Search for Time Variation of the Fine Structure Constant
refs.author: Webb

ext.text: Constants are local near dimensional boundaries. Terra measured and corrected for this long before 2068.

p-webb.detail: Webb and colleagues compared absorption lines of different elements in light from distant quasars, light that records the fine-structure constant as it was billions of years ago, and reported a tiny shift. Later surveys found possible patterns across the sky and possible systematic errors; the question is open. The codex turns the open question into a fact of its world.

tagFrom.sec: VARIABLE CONSTANTS, The Problem [ESTABLISHED → SF TERRITORY]

p-sondhauss.title: Heat makes sound
p-sondhauss.claim: A tube heated at one end can sustain an acoustic oscillation by itself: heat drives sound.

refs.title: Ueber die Schallschwingungen der Luft in erhitzten Glasröhren und in gedeckten Pfeifen von ungleicher Weite
refs.author: Sondhauss

p-sondhauss.detail: Glassblowers had long noticed that a hot bulb on a narrow tube can sing. Sondhauss studied the effect systematically and showed that the pitch follows the tube’s length and the bulb’s volume. Heat added where the gas is compressed and taken away where it expands feeds the oscillation. A heated tube is the simplest heat engine with no moving parts, and the codex makes it the first link of Kha-Ren’s thermoacoustic chain, about 8,350 years before Sondhauss.

tagFrom.sec: B. FIVE TECHNOLOGY DERIVATION CHAINS [ESTABLISHED physics]

p-thermo.title: A heat engine made of sound
p-thermo.claim: A travelling-wave thermoacoustic engine with no moving parts reached 30 percent thermal efficiency, 41 percent of the Carnot limit. Driven the other way, the same cycle pumps heat and cools.

refs.title: A thermoacoustic Stirling heat engine
refs.author: Backhaus

ext.text: The codex caps Kha-Ren bronze engines at 15 to 25 percent of Carnot and scales them to city-wide cooling.

p-thermo.detail: Backhaus and Swift built a looped tube in which the sound wave travels around a ring and passes through a regenerator in the right phase to run a Stirling cycle, with no pistons or valves. Their engine reached 30 percent thermal efficiency, comparable with the petrol engines of its day.

p-kundt.title: Standing waves made visible
p-kundt.claim: Fine powder in a resonating tube collects at the nodes of the standing wave, where the air does not move.

refs.title: Ueber eine neue Art akustischer Staubfiguren
refs.author: Kundt

p-kundt.sec: The First Century: Engagement, the frost patterns
p-kundt.detail: Kundt sprinkled fine powder in a glass tube, set the air inside resonating, and saw the powder gather into regular heaps at the nodes, where the air does not move: a direct way to measure the speed of sound in a gas. Around the artifact the codex has ice do the same. Frost settles where the air is still and is swept from where it oscillates, so the standing wave is drawn on the ground.

p-helmres.title: A bank of resonators is a spectrum analyser
p-helmres.claim: Each tuned resonator answers one frequency, so a set of them splits a sound into its components.

refs.cite: Helmholtz (1863), Die Lehre von den Tonempfindungen (a book; it has no DOI)

p-helmres.sec: C2.5 Empirical Fourier via Helmholtz resonator banks

p-energy.title: Energy is conserved
p-energy.claim: Work and heat are the same quantity in different forms, at a fixed exchange rate; energy can change form but the total stays fixed.

refs.cite: Joule (1850), Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society 140, 61
refs.title: III. On the mechanical equivalent of heat
refs.author: Joule

ext.text: The artifact puts out 58 to 70 kW without stopping: 1.8 kW of sound into the air, about 50 kW into the rock, and 6 to 18 kW holding its cold. Nothing goes in. The codex calls this its single fictional axiom.

p-energy.sec: A. THE ARTIFACT, Total energy output
p-energy.detail: Joule stirred water with paddles driven by falling weights and measured how much warmer it became, showing that a fixed amount of work always makes the same amount of heat. That measurement is the experimental footing of the first law of thermodynamics.

tagFrom.sec: B. FIVE TECHNOLOGY DERIVATION CHAINS [ESTABLISHED physics]

p-axiom.title: The single fictional axiom
p-axiom.claim: The Kha-Ren codex allows itself one impossible thing: the artifact’s energy has no source in its world. Everything downstream of that is meant to be real physics.
p-axiom.sec: A. THE ARTIFACT, Total energy output

p-acoustic.title: 138 dB from a three-metre sphere
p-acoustic.claim: Sound pressure level fixes the intensity at the surface, I = p²/ρc, and the surface area fixes the power.
p-acoustic.sec: A. THE ARTIFACT, SPL at surface
p-acoustic.detail: The decibel scale is logarithmic: every 20 dB is a factor of ten in pressure, so 138 dB is a swing of about 159 pascals, roughly eight million times the threshold of hearing at 20 micropascals. Spread over the surface of a three-metre sphere, that intensity carries about 1.7 kilowatts of sound, close to the codex’s stated 1.8 kW, so its numbers hold together.

p-110.title: Does 110 Hz change how the brain works?
p-110.claim: A pilot study of 30 people reported that 110 Hz tones shifted activity away from left-temporal language areas. It has not been independently replicated. The codex itself grades it low and builds instead on sturdier effects such as group neural synchronisation.

refs.cite: Cook, Pajot & Leuchter (2008), Time and Mind 1, 95
refs.title: Ancient Architectural Acoustic Resonance Patterns and Regional Brain Activity
refs.author: Cook

p-110.sec: A. THE ARTIFACT, 110 Hz neurological effect

p-stone.title: Stone is faster than air
p-stone.claim: Compressional waves cross dense limestone at about 6,000 m/s. Sound in air at 20 °C travels at 343 m/s.
p-stone.detail: Sound travels faster in stiff, dense rock than in air because the restoring force between neighbouring particles is far stronger. Seismologists use these compressional waves, called P waves, to locate earthquakes. A signal tapped into limestone reaches a listener with an ear to the rock long before a shout arrives through the air, and loses less of its energy on the way, which is what the codex’s corridor network relies on.

tagFrom.sec: C. CORRIDOR NETWORK [ESTABLISHED physics, THEORETICAL for scale]

p-kitaev.title: Topological protection
p-kitaev.claim: Information stored in global, non-local topological properties resists local errors.

refs.title: Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons
refs.author: Kitaev

ext.text: Haven has more than three spatial dimensions, and the codex grounds its stability in this kind of protection.

p-kitaev.detail: Kitaev proposed storing quantum information in the collective state of many particles arranged with a particular topology, so that no local disturbance can change it: to corrupt the information an error would have to stretch across the whole system. This is the basis of topological quantum computing, still being built in laboratories. The codex uses the idea to explain why Haven, which has more room than three dimensions, holds still.

p-vortex.title: Chaotic substrate
p-vortex.claim: In the codex the Vortex is a higher-dimensional geometry under ordinary space whose physics is chaotic because something is active in it. It extends the bulk of brane cosmology; no real physics describes its contents.

p-unified.title: Unified Thought
p-unified.claim: In the codex, a change in local physics, made by the artifact’s influence, that alters how consciousness works and lets people think together at very large scale. It is the series’ own invention; no real physics grounds it.

p-82.title: The 8.2 ka event
p-82.claim: Greenland ice cores record an abrupt, widespread cold event about 8,200 years ago.

refs.title: Holocene climatic instability: A prominent, widespread event 8200 yr ago
refs.author: Alley

p-82.detail: The event appears in the Greenland ice cores as an abrupt drop in temperature, and in climate records around the North Atlantic. It is usually linked to a sudden release of glacial meltwater into the ocean, which weakened the currents that carry heat north. The codex makes it the cold, dry pressure under which Kha-Ren’s social order hardened into castes.

p-42.title: The 4.2 ka event
p-42.claim: Abrupt aridification around 2200 BCE coincides with the abandonment of settlements on the Habur plains of northern Mesopotamia.

refs.title: The Genesis and Collapse of Third Millennium North Mesopotamian Civilization
refs.author: Weiss

p-42.detail: Weiss and colleagues dated the abandonment of Tell Leilan and other sites on the Habur plains to an abrupt drying around 2200 BCE, and later records from lakes, caves and the ocean show a widespread climate shift at about the same time; how widespread and how sharp is still argued. The codex keeps the event in Kha-Ren’s world, where it forces irrigation and food preservation and makes Kha-Ren a refuge.

p-higgs.title: The Higgs boson
p-higgs.claim: A new boson near 125 GeV is observed independently by two experiments at the Large Hadron Collider.

refs.title: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson
refs.author: Aad

refs.title: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV
refs.author: Chatrchyan

p-higgs.detail: The Higgs boson was the last particle the Standard Model predicted and had not yet seen; its discovery completed the model nearly fifty years after the mechanism was proposed. Since then the Large Hadron Collider has found no new fundamental particle. The codex extrapolates that drought forward: in its 2068 two larger colliders have confirmed the Standard Model and found nothing new, the despair Book 1 opens into.

p-age.title: How old is the Earth?
p-age.claim: Radiometric dating of meteorites and the oldest minerals puts the Earth’s age at about 4.54 billion years, within about one percent.

refs.cite: Dalrymple (2001), Geological Society, London, Special Publications 190, 205
refs.title: The age of the Earth in the twentieth century: a problem (mostly) solved
refs.author: Dalrymple

p-hublin.title: How old is our species?
p-hublin.claim: Fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco, place early Homo sapiens at about 300,000 years ago.

refs.title: New fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco and the pan-African origin of Homo sapiens
refs.author: Hublin

p-holocene.title: Dating the Holocene
p-holocene.claim: The base of the Holocene is set in the Greenland NGRIP ice core at 11,700 years before 2000 CE.

refs.cite: Walker et al. (2009), Journal of Quaternary Science 24, 3
refs.title: Formal definition and dating of the GSSP for the base of the Holocene
refs.author: Walker
